name: The Iva Valley shooting

summary.text: Enugu, capital of the Eastern Region from 1938, grew around the government coal mines, which employed about 6,000 men in 1948, most of them from Udi. Conditions were harsh, with beatings, humiliations and irregular pay, and in late 1949 the miners of the Iva Valley mine believed large sums of arrears were being withheld from them, a belief fed by the nationalist ‘Zikist’ press. On 18 November 1949 police under a British superintendent, F. S. Philip, fired on the unarmed strikers, killing 21 and wounding 51. The shooting fired nationalist feeling across Nigeria, above all in the East: pro-Zikist unions formed the National Emergency Committee, which spread word of the killings and organised meetings, demonstrations and riots against colonial rule.

moments.title: The strike
moments.text: The Iva Valley miners strike over the arrears they believe the management is withholding.

moments.title: The shooting
moments.text: Superintendent F. S. Philip orders his British and Nigerian police to fire on the unarmed miners: 21 are killed and 51 wounded.

moments.title: The National Emergency Committee
moments.text: Unions sympathetic to the Zikists and the NCNC form the National Emergency Committee, which carries news of the killings across Nigeria and organises protests and riots.
